module.title: Phantom self-gravity, sink particles and N-body
entrypoints: SETUP=binary phantomsetup+phantom (official v2025.0.0 release binary workflow)
module.expensive_path: The kd-tree gravity walk in src/main/kdtree.F90 (compute_M2L / expand_fgrav_in_taylor_series / the FMM node walk) driven from src/main/force.F90. In the Evrard collapse at 103806 particles the timing block attributes 70% of step time to force (which carries the tree gravity) and 28% to density, with the tree build itself only 1.3%. The sink-sink and sink-gas force loops in src/main/ptmass.F90 plus the adaptive substepping dominate the sink-only workloads instead, and those are effectively serial.
module.rationale: Self-gravity, sink particles and N-body form one coherent code path: the kd-tree serves both the SPH gravity and (with SINKTREE) the sinks, ptmass.F90 supplies sink-sink/sink-gas gravity and the substepping that the N-body tests exercise, and utils_orbits/set_binary/set_hierarchical are the initial-condition and diagnostic layer shared by every sink and N-body test. The expanded survey retains every suitable official selector and adds the official release binary example, giving 21 checks rather than treating a three-minute survey timeout as a scientific exclusion.
excluded: pure hydro and the shock/wave/turbulence setups (phantom-hd-turbulence)
MHD and non-ideal MHD, including SETUP=jet which is the only gravity-enabled sphereinbox variant (phantom-mhd-nonideal)
GR: SETUP=testgr, test_ptmass test_sink_binary_gr (selector ptmassgenrel), test_externf_gr (phantom-relativity-spacetime)
ptmassHII / test_HIIregion: sink radiative feedback, better owned by a feedback module
SETUP=solarsystem: needs MPC data from the network
SETUP=cluster / sphereinbox / collidingclouds: need data/velfield/cube_v[123].dat, downloaded at runtime
SETUP=starcluster: needs clusterbin.txt from the empty, Zenodo-backed data/starcluster
SETUP=binarybh: GR=yes (relativity module) and needs an empty, Zenodo-backed data/binarybh trajectory file
hazards: build/.depends does not exist: no Fortran module dependencies are expressed, so `make -j` fails and a failed parallel build leaves .o without .mod (build/ must be wiped). Build with -j1 and ONE goal per invocation - `make phantom setup` in one call makes them clean each other.

One SETUP per build tree; this module needs both SETUP=testgrav and SETUP=testsinktree, i.e. two full phantomtest builds, plus one build per evolved setup (~80 s phantom, ~15 s setup, ~115 s phantomtest uncontended).

Under SETUP=test the 'gravity' selector prints TEST SUITE PASSED with ZERO assertions (no -DGRAVITY), and a selector matching nothing runs the whole suite: build SETUP=testgrav/testsinktree and require a positive denominator in the parsed 'PASSED: n of m'.
Dump headers embed a wall-clock date/time stamp (readwrite_dumps_common.f90 fileident, bytes 0x24-0x87), so whole-dump cmp always differs; compare array by array (inv/infra/tools/phantom_dump.py).
nfulldump defaults to 10, so every intermediate dump is a float32 'small dump' with no poten; any evolved-dump check must set nfulldump=1.

poten is real(kind=4) in memory (part.F90:252) and float32 on disk; h, dt, alpha, divv are also float32; density is not stored at all (derived from h, hence float32). Only x,y,z, vxyzu and all sink arrays are binary64.

Self-gravity SPH evolution is NOT bit-reproducible above one thread, and the divergence onset moves earlier as threads increase: an Evrard collapse at 21982 particles is identical across two 1-thread runs through 83 steps, agrees through nmax=40 but not nmax=83 at 2 threads, and already differs at nmax=40 at 4 threads (x 3.0e-5). Infra's Sedov hydro result (bit-identical across 1/2/4 threads) does NOT carry over to the gravity tree. A short window alone cannot make an evolved self-gravity dump bit-comparable on an accelerator; the check needs a calibrated tolerance.

phantom rewrites the .in in place after each full dump (logfile -> NN+1, dumpfile -> last dump), so re-running ./phantom <prefix>.in in the same directory restarts from the last dump instead of t=0. Regenerate the .in or use a fresh directory for every graded run.

dtwallmax (default 024:00 in the generated .in) lets the measured wall time of the previous dump interval halve dtmax and force nfulldump=1 (evolve.F90:213,318 -> dynamic_dtmax.f90:157). Pin dtwallmax = 000:00 and twallmax = 000:00 in every graded .in so a slow target cannot take a different timestep path from the oracle.

Sink-only N-body showed 20x worse wall time at 2 threads than at 1 with cpu/wall = 0.08 in the substep timer, but that was measured at host load 300-400 and is confounded by contention (GOMP spin-wait on an oversubscribed machine); re-measure on an idle host. Either way a 5-sink no-gas workload has no parallelism worth claiming, and ptmasschinchen is similarly serial.
phantomtest allocates 1.18 GB at start (maxp=1e6); phantomsetup allocates ~1.9 GB. Give the checks at least 2 GB. phantomsetup must be run twice (1st pass writes the .setup and exits).

The fresh serial native survey corrected earlier overloaded-host timing: ptmasschinchen finishes in 1.66 s (2/2 assertions) and ptmassSDAR in 58.89 s (8/8). ptmassbinary and the SETUP=testsinktree sinktree selector reached the three-minute survey cap without completing; this means runtime is unmeasured, not that the physics is unsuitable. Their windows are compiled into the upstream tests.

At the pinned source testsuite.f90 omits dosinktree from the doany expression. Therefore `phantomtest sinktree` under SETUP=testsinktree enters the aggregate suite before its explicit sinktree rerun. The benchmark preserves and discloses this exact official behaviour; it is expensive and duplicates assertions, but it is also the only official SINKTREE coverage.

The official binary-release workflow downloads four v2025.0.0 assets. The benchmark vendors the two 8-9 MB MESA profiles plus the small release decks under the check, with hashes matching .github/workflows/binary.yml, so the graded run remains offline and reproducible.

Several data/ subdirectories ship EMPTY and are curl-fetched from Zenodo at runtime (src/main/datafiles.f90:70-100): data/velfield (13162515) blocks SETUP=cluster/sphereinbox/jet/collidingclouds; data/starcluster (13164858) blocks SETUP=starcluster; data/binarybh (18615172) blocks SETUP=binarybh; data/eos/{mesa,mesa_opac,helmholtz,lombardi}, data/forcing and data/galaxy_merger are empty too. data/star_data_files, data/orbits, data/neutronstar and data/galcen ARE populated, so evrard/polytrope/hierarchical are unaffected.
SETUP=evrard ignores the --np= command-line flag: np1 lives in the .setup file and must be edited there.
SETUP=polytrope relaxes both stars by default (26 s) and drops relax1*/relax2* .ev/.profile/dump files into the run directory.
ptmass tests write fort.NNN and Sink00.sink into the CWD; deleted at the end of a complete run but they survive a kill.

All wall times in this investigation were taken on a host at load 300-400 and are upper bounds; the bitwise-comparison results are load-independent. SETUP=hierarchical determinism at 4 threads and its runtime above 2 threads remain unmeasured.
